guide.title: Suction
guide.lead: If you hear gurgling, suction now. Insert the catheter without suction, suction only as you withdraw, keep each pass short, and re-oxygenate between passes. Watch the heart rate, especially in children.

sections.title: Which catheter
rows: Mouth and oropharynx; thick secretions, vomit
Nose; through an adjunct or tube

sections.title: Technique

steps.title: Measure
steps.text: Corner of the mouth to the earlobe; never beyond what you can see.

steps.title: Keep it short
steps.text: Adult 15 seconds, child 10 seconds, infant 5 seconds per pass.

steps.title: Re-oxygenate
steps.text: Ventilate or oxygenate between passes; watch heart rate and SpO₂.

sections.after: Vomiting with no spinal concern: roll the patient onto the side first.

items.label: Sinus bradycardia
items.sub: Vagal response or hypoxia during suction: stop and oxygenate

quiz.q: Maximum suction time per attempt in an adult:

quiz.explanation: Oxygen is removed and the vagus stimulated.

quiz.q: Maximum suction time per attempt in an infant:
Best catheter for thick vomit in the mouth:
quiz.explanation: Soft catheters for the nose and tubes.

quiz.q: How deep do you insert a rigid catheter?
options: No further than you can see (corner of mouth to earlobe)

quiz.q: Heart rate drops during infant suction. You:
A soft (French) catheter is best for:
options: The nose and suctioning through a tube

quiz.q: Patient vomits; no spinal concern. Quickest way to clear the airway?
options: Roll onto the side, then suction

flashcards.question: When to apply suction
flashcards.answer: Only while withdrawing; insert without suction.

flashcards.question: Maximum time per pass
flashcards.answer: Adult 15 seconds, child 10 seconds, infant 5 seconds.

flashcards.question: Measuring depth
flashcards.answer: Corner of the mouth to the earlobe; never beyond what you can see.

flashcards.question: Complications of prolonged suction
flashcards.answer: Hypoxia and vagal bradycardia, especially in children.

flashcards.question: Vomiting, no spinal concern
flashcards.answer: Roll onto the side, then suction.

critical.scenario: A patient vomits during BVM ventilation; the airway fills with fluid.
critical.question: Immediate action?

options.t: Stop, roll the patient (no spinal concern) or suction until clear, then resume

critical.kpi: Prioritizes airway clearance over continued ventilation

critical.scenario: While suctioning an infant's airway for 20 seconds, the heart rate falls from 140 to 80.
critical.question: What happened and what do you do?

options.t: Vagal bradycardia / hypoxia: stop, oxygenate or ventilate; limit infant passes to 5 seconds
Keep suctioning: the airway must be clear

options.f: Ventilate first; CPR if HR stays below 60 with poor perfusion.

critical.kpi: Recognizes suction-induced bradycardia and limits attempt time

critical.scenario: You're about to suction an adult's mouth and aren't sure how deep to go.
critical.question: How do you decide?

options.t: Measure from the corner of the mouth to the earlobe and stay in the visible field
Same as an NPA length, past the tongue
